common.name: Name
common.changesApplyNextSlide: Changes take effect from the next slideshow transition.
common.changesApplySoon: Changes take effect in the slideshow within a few seconds.

settings.title: Slideshow settings
settings.languageDescription: Language used by the admin UI and slideshow overlays.
settings.clientPresenceDetectionDescription: Pause the shared slideshow timeline while no slideshow display is connected.
settings.slideshowZoomDescription: Browser-like zoom level for the slideshow display. 1.0 means 100%.
settings.timeZoneDescription: Used for night mode and calendar overlay schedules.
settings.transitionEffectsDescription: Select multiple effects to rotate between them. 'Random' uses all effects and excludes specific choices.
settings.cinematicChanceDescription: Randomly applies a cinematic teal-and-orange color look to some images. The transition is always a fade in that case.
settings.avoidRepeats: Repeat shown photos only after a full pass
settings.avoidRepeatsDescription: When enabled, never-shown photos are preferred; already-shown photos return only after all photos were shown once.
settings.groupPortraitsDescription: When enabled, 3-portrait slides prefer neighboring photos from the source folder. When disabled, all three are picked randomly.
settings.photoFrameDescription: Subtle visual frame around each displayed photo.
settings.caption: Timestamp and location
settings.captionDescription: Position of the photo caption in the slideshow.
settings.grainDescription: Fine film-grain texture as a global overlay over the whole slideshow.
settings.nightModeDescription: Shows a blank screen instead of photos outside the configured time span. The queue resumes exactly where it left off.
settings.autoRescanDescription: Scans all non-paused sources once per day automatically, in addition to manual rescans.
settings.enableCollagesDescription: Occasionally combines photos taken close together in time, for example an afternoon on vacation, into one shared view.
settings.timeWindowDescription: How close capture times must be for photos to land in the same collage.
settings.layoutTypesDescription: Which of the 10 collage layouts may appear. 'Random' uses all layouts and excludes specific choices.

collages.heroWithSupporting: Hero image with supporting photos (8 photos)

sources.title: Sources
sources.deleteConfirm: Do you really want to delete source "{{name}}"? All related photos will be removed from the slideshow.
sources.locationBackfillStarted: Location lookup started in the background.

date.title: Date
date.showDescription: Shows the current date and time in the top-right corner of the slideshow.
date.behaviorDescription: On some photos, the date fades in softly and then fades out again.

weather.title: Weather
weather.showDescription: Shows current weather and forecast in the slideshow.
weather.locationDescription: Please select a suggested location. Free text is not saved.
weather.behaviorDescription: On some photos, weather fades in together with the date.
weather.attribution: Weather data comes from Open-Meteo. The location is validated via Open-Meteo Geocoding.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.connectAccountFirst: Connect an account first to select calendars.
calendar.noCalendars: No calendars found yet — sync is running.
calendar.deleteConfirm: Do you really want to disconnect account "{{label}}"? All related calendars and cached events will be removed.
calendar.showOverlayDescription: Shows today's events as an overlay over the slideshow while the current time is inside the configured period.
calendar.label: Label
calendar.applePasswordHelp: Create one at appleid.apple.com under Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords. Do not use your normal Apple ID password.
calendar.googleIntro: Google requires each application to have its own registered OAuth client ID before it may request calendar access. This is a one-time setup step for this Fotify installation. Users later approve access on Google, without entering a password into Fotify.
calendar.googleStep1: Open Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials and create a project, or select an existing one.
calendar.googleStep2: Under APIs & Services → Library, search for Google Calendar API and enable it.
calendar.googleStep3: Under OAuth consent screen, create an external consent screen and add the calendar.readonly scope. While the app is in Testing, add your own Google account as a test user.
calendar.googleStep4: Under Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth client ID, choose Web application.
calendar.googleStep5: Enter exactly this address as Authorized redirect URI. It updates when the public address below changes:
calendar.publicUrlDescription: Only the base address without path, e.g. {{origin}}. Do not enter the full redirect URI above; /calendar/google/callback is appended automatically.
calendar.afterSetupText: Click Connect to Google. This opens the Google sign-in page. After confirming there, the account is connected automatically.
